source.title: EnsemW2S: Enhancing Weak-to-Strong Generalization with Large Language Model Ensembles
source.authors: Aakriti Agrawal; Mucong Ding; Chenghao Deng; Zora Che; Arjun Rajaram; Anirudh Satheesh; Bang An; C. Bruss; John Langford; Fu-Rong Huang

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present. Some appendix tables are flattened, and plotted results do not provide exact numerical PGR values in the text.
record.tranche_reason: Tests weak-to-strong training and reports PGR-related outcomes, but its main intervention is an ensemble of iteratively reweighted weak supervisors rather than the original single-supervisor setup.
record.gate_note: The paper reports PGR plots for model-size sweeps and SciQ, with only qualitative descriptions for several plots. The rows below include the separately tabulated Qwen results, the Quartz model-pair results in Table 5, and text-described SciQ outcomes. Theoretical training-error and margin statements concern the weak-model ensemble, not a condition proving that a strong student must beat its supervisor.
record.test_reason: Proposes an ensemble (EnsemW2S/AdaBoost) of weak supervisors. It reports weak, naive weak-to-strong, ensemble weak-to-strong and oracle accuracy for Qwen2.5 3B→7B (Table 1), Pythia pairs on Quartz (Table 5) and GPT-2/Qwen pairs on SciQ (Burns et al. code, App. J.3). Its own results bear on V1, V2, V3 and V4.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that iteratively boosted token-level ensembles of weak experts give better supervision, improving the strong student on ID and OOD (easy-hard, cross-dataset) data. They claim gains up to 3.2% ID and 2.42% OOD, and complete W2S generalization in some binary SciQ pairs. The 'far from full capability' caveat and the no-gain pairs are specific to SciQ easy-hard (very small and GPT-2-xl+ pairs) and to models too small to learn.
record.recipe_differences: Uses weak labels to fine-tune stronger students and reports PGR, but improves the weak supervisors by token-level AdaBoost-inspired ensembling and also studies easy-to-hard and cross-dataset settings; includes the easy labeled data in some student-training runs.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary with model pair and data split; the paper reports that very small models can fail to show meaningful gains and that easy-hard SciQ gains do not occur for specified small and large pairs.

fits_no_version.finding: Ensembles of weak experts (Qwen2.5-1.5B/3B) gain 0.4–6% accuracy over single experts on ID and OOD data. An equal-weight 5-model baseline does not help (Fig. 3, Table 2).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Boosted ensembles of weak LLMs generalize better than single weak models trained on the same data.

record.peer_reviewed: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (as provided in the study metadata); the paper text itself does not identify proceedings details.
record.problems: Exact PGR values for the main Pythia sweeps are available only in plots, not stated numerically in the text. Several appendix tables are flattened and report multiple token/option metrics. The authors note that weak and strong models are proxies for human- and superhuman-level systems, and that the experiments cover only supervised fine-tuning. Some Qwen entries exceed the listed oracle value.
record.rows_left_out: Appendix Tables 3, 4, 6 and 7 contain additional Pythia pair-level token-average, option-accuracy, and student-training metrics. They are not transcribed here because the flattened column layout makes pairing the multiple metrics to each model-pair row unreliable; the selected Quartz model-pair results are reported separately in Table 5. Figure 12 repeats the ARC generation sweep qualitatively, and exact plotted PGR values are not stated.

untested.parts: Single-supervisor setup without gold labels in student training for Qwen (the student also sees the labelled half or easy data). Pythia naive PGR values are not readable from rows.
Auxiliary confidence loss and other loss variants.
Chess and reward modelling. Representation-based predictors. Size-dependence of PGR is plotted but not numerically readable.
Students exploiting what the supervisor cannot check. Shared weak/strong error patterns.
Not tested: the theory covers only training-error decay of the weak ensemble.
No vision or other non-language modality.

missing.what: Pythia Quartz/ARC weak option accuracy, naive and ensemble W2S option accuracy, and oracle accuracy (3 seeds, SEM). These would allow V1 PGR per pair. A tentative reading suggests naive W2S is at or below weak accuracy in larger Quartz random pairs (e.g. 1.4B→2.8B: weak 69.64, W2S 67.94).
Text claim that model capability, not size, predicts PGR (Qwen-1.8B vs GPT-2-xl).
Average SciQ improvement of 6.52% on the random split (only easy-hard 3% recorded in F5).

record.verdict_notes: PGR values here are computed from Table 1 accuracies. The Qwen student training includes gold-labelled data (the ID half or easy set), unlike Burns et al., so V1/V4 numbers are confounded. The Pythia Table 5 sweep is single-run, gives no weak/oracle values, and many values sit near the 50% chance level of 2-option Quartz. Q7's student exceeds the oracle.

versions.untested_parts: Tests weak-to-strong students under ensemble-generated weak labels; does not establish the effect for all tasks or for the original single weak-supervisor setup.
Tests ensemble weak supervisors against a single-supervisor baseline; does not test auxiliary confidence loss or the other loss variants named in the claim.
Tests model sizes, multiple-choice QA and binary classification, and ID/easy-hard/cross-dataset settings. Does not test chess, reward modelling, or representation-based predictors.
Tests easy-hard and cross-dataset shifts, but not supervisor-checkability exploits or whether shared error patterns explain reduced gains.
The paper gives a theoretical bound for training error of its weak ensemble; it does not give conditions under which a strong student must beat its supervisor.
No vision or other non-language modality is tested.

source_check.notes: The supplied manuscript is arXiv v1 dated 28 May 2025, contrary to the record's 2024 year. Table 1 and Section 6.2 disagree on the Math-MC easy-hard gain and swap the elementary/high-school MMLU gain descriptions; Table 5 is single-run, while other appendix tables report three-run SEM.

statements.correction: Sections 3.1 and 3.3: binary AdaBoost reweights examples and aggregates weighted classifier votes; token-level EnsemW2S addresses generation. Appendix J.3: GPT-2-medium→large random-split PGR exceeds 100%.
statements.problem: The SciQ experiment uses binary-classification AdaBoost; token-level ensembling does not describe this experiment's distinguishing method.

statements.correction: Table 1: Qwen student accuracy gains span 1.00–3.88 points; ID gains are 1.96, 3.15 and 2.10 points. Table 5: all-pair relative improvements span 0–9.1% random and 0.9–7.8% easy-hard. Appendix J.3: SciQ average improvements are 6.52% random and 3% easy-hard.
statements.problem: The Qwen gain range omits Math-MC easy-hard; the Pythia range describes selected pairs rather than all Quartz results.

statements.correction: S10: Quartz random, Pythia-410M→1B, 0.551→0.551. Q4: ARC easy-hard, Qwen2.5-3B→7B, accuracy 45.39→46.67; own-supervisor PGR approximately 0.292→0.168.
statements.problem: The cited rows from this study are not described, and their Quartz/ARC conditions are absent from the stated conditions.

statements.correction: SciQ uses binary AdaBoost with example weighting and weighted classifier voting. Average accuracy improvement: 6.52% random, 3% easy-hard; GPT-2-medium→large random PGR exceeds 100%; some easy-hard pairs show no improvement.
statements.problem: Token-level ensembling is incorrectly presented as the method distinction for the binary SciQ comparison.

statements.correction: Section 5: ID students train on pseudo-labelled data plus the initially gold-labelled half; easy-hard students train on pseudo-labelled hard data plus gold-labelled easy data. Table 1 computed naive PGR: ARC approximately 0.507→0.292; Quartz approximately 0.491→0.353.
statements.problem: The PGR calculations are correct, but describing the Qwen setup simply as naive training on weak labels omits direct gold supervision.

statements.correction: Table 1 supervisor: Qwen2.5-3B. Section 5: Qwen students train on both gold labels and pseudo-labels. Computed naive PGR: ARC 0.507→0.292; Quartz 0.491→0.353; Math-MC 0.281→0.819; MMLU 0.586, 0.648 and 0.897.
statements.problem: The numerical comparisons are correct, but the closing description of both studies as naive weak-label fine-tuning omits this study's direct gold supervision.

statements.correction: Table 1: Qwen student gains span 1.00–3.88 points; Section 6.2 instead reports 1.17 points for Math-MC easy-hard.
